title: Scenes: robots on editable terrain with long command lists, simulated on the surrogate and recorded as video
summary: The viewer gains a Scene page. A scene is a terrain built from features (box, ramp, steps, bump, noise) and one or more robots, each with a checkpoint, a start and a command list of any length. The page edits a scene and shows where each robot's commands lead; locomotion.surrogate.scene runs every robot on the surrogate with the terrain as a MuJoCo height field; viewer/scene_view.py writes the result; and the page plays it, drawing each robot as the Runs page does, and records it as a WebM video. SurrogateEnv takes an optional terrain and start pose for this; without them it is unchanged. Robots run on separate copies of the terrain and pass through each other, the touchdown model is off on terrain because it assumes a flat floor, and the policies were trained on flat ground, so a scene is a design tool, not evidence.
next: Use scenes to film the destination_v29 model on terrain and to look for where blind walking fails.
reason: A viewer page and surrogate tooling for videos; training, the canonical task, reward and evaluator are unchanged, and SurrogateEnv without a terrain or start is unchanged.
